title: Error Handling: catchError, retry, and throwError

questions.prompt: What happens to a stream when one of its operator callbacks throws?

options.text: The stream emits a terminal error and stops — no further next or complete
The value is skipped and the stream continues
The error is logged but ignored
The stream restarts automatically

questions.explanation: Errors are terminal. The stream sends an error notification, stops, and tears down. Recovery requires catchError or retry.

options.text: A new Observable — e.g., of(fallback), EMPTY, or throwError(() => err)
A plain value to emit
Nothing; it just logs the error
A Promise only

questions.explanation: catchError replaces the errored stream with the Observable you return: of(x) to recover, EMPTY to swallow, or throwError to rethrow.

questions.prompt: In a search pipeline, why put `catchError` INSIDE the `switchMap` rather than after it?

options.text: So a single failed request is recovered without killing the outer search stream
Because catchError cannot appear at the top level of a pipe
To make requests run in parallel
It makes no difference where it goes

questions.explanation: Catching inside the inner Observable isolates the failure to that request. Outside the switchMap, the first error terminates the whole outer stream, so the search box stops responding.

questions.prompt: What does `retry(2)` do on an erroring source?

options.text: Resubscribes to the source up to 2 more times (3 attempts total) before forwarding the error
Delays the error by 2 seconds
Emits the last value twice
Ignores the error permanently

questions.explanation: retry(n) resubscribes to the (cold) source on error up to n times. Because it re-runs the producer, it re-fires side effects like HTTP requests.

questions.prompt: This retry operator is deprecated in RxJS 7.8 in favor of `retry({ delay })`. Type its name.
questions.explanation: retryWhen is deprecated. Use the config form retry({ count, delay }) with a notifier for custom/backoff retry timing.

questions.prompt: Which are sound error-handling practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Retry with a max count and backoff for transient failures
Only retry idempotent operations
Return of(fallback) or EMPTY from catchError to keep a stream alive
Retry every POST request infinitely by default

questions.explanation: Bounded retries with backoff, retrying only idempotent operations, and graceful fallbacks are all good. Infinite retries on non-idempotent writes can cause duplicate side effects.
